messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: Minimun number of sightings for a robust analysis
parts:
If you are prepared to assume a common detection function across
treatments, the small sample size isn't unduly problematic - though the
test would then be rather redundant give the huge difference in
encounter rates! Of course, you then have to cope with the correlation
between the two density estimates, as described in the intro to ds
book. In fact, even if the detection functions differ, you MAY be able
to do something useful, by using the mcds engine in Distance. If you
have covariates that allow you to model the difference in detectability
between habitats, then you have a single detection function model across
the treatments, while allowing detectability to vary.

Steve
